target_customer: Grocery retailers and consumers buying leafy greens and herbs grown in robotic hydroponic greenhouses
problem: Conventional agriculture has heavy environmental impact and labor dependence; Iron Ox aimed to grow produce year-round in automated greenhouses using robots and plant data.
business_model: Vertically integrated grower selling produce to retailers, with robotics technology; later shifted toward technology for growers

founders.name: Brandon Alexander
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch author profile says he grew up on a family farm and worked in robotics at Willow Garage and then Google (https://techcrunch.com/author/brandon-alexander). Education not found.

founders.name: Jonathan Binney
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO with no background; no bio source opened.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as inactive. TechCrunch reported 50 layoffs in November 2022 and the company said it was not winding down. One low-quality page claims a Chapter 7 filing in August 2023; not corroborated.

competitors.name: AeroFarms
competitors.what: Indoor aeroponic vertical farming of baby leafy greens, building a large Newark, New Jersey farm
competitors.traction_then: Newark farm under construction in late 2015, with two more US farms planned for 2016
competitors.funding_then: $20M financing in December 2015 led by Wheatsheaf Group (AgFunderNews calls it a Series B; about $33M equity raised in total)

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed robotic arms, mobile plant-moving carts, vision and plant science combined in a working automated greenhouse, which is research-grade robotics plus agronomy and capital intensive construction.

defensibility.rationale: Custom robotics and growth data were hard to copy and the company held IRON OX trademarks, but the product (leafy greens) was a commodity and capital intensity favored well funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it directly. Peers raised far larger sums later (Plenty reportedly over $940M, Bowery $300M Series C), which pressured a smaller competitor on capital.

market_need_then: Water use, labor cost and long supply chains for fresh produce were widely discussed in 2015 and 2016, and AeroFarms had just raised $20M. Iron Ox's own mission statement frames farming's environmental impact as the problem; no 2016 demand data specific to Iron Ox was found.

branding.domain_note: Operated as ironox.com in its public years; the YC record now lists inevitabletech.com.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: Robotics plus greenhouse imagery in press coverage
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, climate framed: 'To make food a renewable resource, for everyone'.

branding.brand_signature: Autonomous robot farm, widely covered as 'America's first robot farm'

rebrands.why: One source says it shifted toward technology for growers; a reason was not confirmed by a company statement.

branding.community_and_virality: Broad press coverage in TechCrunch, MIT Technology Review and others for its robot farm launch in 2018 and for its 2021 round.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press attention for a small startup and registered IRON OX trademarks, but no evidence of consumer brand loyalty or that the brand drove growth.

pivots.from: Operating its own robotic greenhouses and selling produce
pivots.to: Technology for growers under the name Inevitable Tech
pivots.why: Reported by a single source; reason not confirmed.

outcome_analysis: Iron Ox raised about $98M by September 2021 and built automated greenhouses, but cut 50 jobs in November 2022, nearly half its staff, citing the need to extend cash runway while saying it was not winding down. The business combined research-grade robotics with capital-heavy greenhouse build-out in a commodity produce market, and the cash runway statement points to running short of money, though the final cause of the inactive status is not documented by a reliable source.
notes: Total raised stated by the press: $45M at the time of the September 2020 round and $98M after the September 2021 Series C; TechCrunch in Nov 2022 said over $100M. Recorded rounds sum to far less than $45M, so about $20M or more of rounds before the Series B (including the 2019 Series A and A-II listed by CB Insights without amounts) are missing. The pre-seed (April 2016, amount reported as $1.5M and $2M in different aggregator results) and the 2018 seed ($3M, startupintros) each rest on a single database or outlet; the 2019 Series A rests on CB Insights alone. The CB Insights page was seen only through search results. The YC page lists the batch as Winter 2016 while one profile says Summer 2015; YC directory used. One page (ideaproof.io) claims an August 2023 Chapter 7 liquidation; no reliable source corroborates it. Company website inevitabletech.com returned empty content when fetched. Brand strength 3 is a judgment from press coverage only.
